title: Sowing and planting A sound start
status: Wide outdoor photographic proof for review
brief: Direct sowing in a row in open soil; module seedlings on the greenhouse bench; planting a hardened-off lettuce plug into open garden soil.
setting: Home garden, at the porch end of the bed facing the greenhouse. John kneels on the lawn for direct sowing and planting out. The module-tray photograph stays in the greenhouse.

outdoor_generation.prompt:
Create ONE matched pair of natural unposed full-figure documentary photographs of the same real gardener John Lennon at work in his own Cornish back garden, as a 2:1 horizontal diptych of two equal square photographs. Hard cut exactly at centre, no border, no text. These are outdoor book photographs for "Direct into the bed" and "Plant them out". A separate greenhouse macro already exists to go between them in the book. Change the visual language completely from a neat anonymous hands close-up: the viewer is now standing a few paces back on the lawn watching John actually garden. In BOTH photos frame his WHOLE BODY comfortably, with visible air beyond his bare head, his back, the knees and seat of his worn jeans, ankles and his entire pair of scuffed gardening boots including the soles/tips. No part of his figure cropped at any image edge. His kneeling body fills approximately 55–62% of the frame height. Make his face recognisable and both jobs readable, with ordinary adult hands to scale. Real garden at its real proportions; include foreground soil, grass path and identifiable outbuildings. Use a normal 40mm documentary lens; quiet natural light, clear environmental detail, no blurred-out portrait background.

Attached real garden photographs 1–2 fix the geography. Position the camera at the porch end looking along John's open growing bed towards the greenhouses. Porch is behind camera. Use the narrow grassy working strip at the left side of the bed, greenhouse to the back-left on its low masonry base, blue shed partly visible farther left, existing raised berry planter with weathered timber, terracotta pots, pale horizontal garden fence on its low weathered masonry and transverse timber beds at rear. Respect the actual bed's long footprint and ground level. The photos show its original construction; now this is a working vegetable bed of dark garden earth. Omit cardboard, current compost heaps and high raised sides. No newly invented structures. Soil shows a fine prepared strip with a few clods elsewhere, tiny stones, fragments of organic matter and a small scatter of compost at its wobbly grass edge. Lawn is mottled spring grass, some clover and flattened blades where knees have rested. Keep the mild disorder and vernacular of the REAL SITE photo, without staging a collection of props. Soft silver UK daylight, normal colour, visual texture where the light touches it. Warm, candid gardening moment; no stock-photo tableau.

Reference 3 is the important lowered-face likeness sheet, reference 5 is the real bareheaded John. Reproduce THIS individual, adult in his 60s, thinning receding grey-brown hair, longer high forehead, slim features, short soft grey beard. The tip of the chin distinctly recedes well behind the lower lip, down and back towards the neck; grey beard follows it and disappears toward the collar when leaning forward. Do not add a pointed or square beard extension. Reference 4 shows two real views of working clothes and build, NOT the scene. No hats, glasses or microphone. Show a natural side or three-quarter view of his lowered face in each photograph, with room to read the expression. He is absorbed in the work, not posing or looking at us.

LEFT photo: earlier cool spring day. John in the oatmeal flecked jumper in the top view of ref 4, faded jeans with soil on knees and worn boots, kneeling on the available grass, tall enough in the composition to clearly see the entire man. Leisurely one knee down, his other leg folded with one boot planted for balance; weight plausibly taken by his legs. In profile facing the bed, he holds a small scruffy, partly open seed envelope in his left hand close to his lap, right hand pinched and held very LOW above a single shallow drill to sow carrot seeds thinly. Follow his hand to the long narrow furrow running away along the bed. The individual seeds are almost too small to see at this distance, never a dotted line of huge seeds. No lettuce in this photograph. Crop action stays legible from the seed packet, wrist gesture and the prepared row.

RIGHT photo: later spring, slightly brighter light, different unposed moment. John in the navy pullover and work jeans from the bottom view of ref 4, scuffed boots, settling back on his heels on the grassy edge, hips turned naturally, both boots and his whole head in frame. Nearby camera offset by a small step, same believable perspective and John at similar scale. Show him lowering a young Little Gem lettuce plug into a snug hole in the open soil; his fingers support the small, square-tapered plug at the root ball and the other hand draws loose soil in. Small ordinary muted young lettuce and two already planted farther down the row at realistic spacings; a part-used black module tray sitting casually on the grass just by his knee to establish where the plug came from. Natural variation in leaf angle and size. Keep body language different from the sowing shot; make each a believable moment a gardening companion happened to photograph while he was working. In both images preserve a little margin around the whole figure at top, sides and bottom. No montage inside either panel, no cutaways, no text, no graphic elements.
